$comment: Content-parity invariants enforced by hooks/multi-provider-consistency-checker. Each entry's text must appear in every listed file. Whitespace is normalised, so line-wrapping may differ between files. Add an entry whenever the agent deliberately restates the same wording in more than one place.

sharedPhrases.name: requirement-type-taxonomy
sharedPhrases.why: The approved requirement types are restated in three places. If they drift, an extractor can classify against a list one file does not recognise — which is how performance requirements were being dropped before they became a first-class type. All eight types are declared, so a change to any one of them breaks the check; this requires the three files to phrase the list identically (word forms, Oxford 'or'), which they now do.
sharedPhrases.text: functional flow, content rule, visual rule, accessibility rule, performance rule, analytics or conversion rule, integration rule, or error or empty state

sharedPhrases.name: pagespeed-agent-routing
sharedPhrases.why: Performance routing is only safe if every surface names the same owner. A file that omits the hand-off invites an invented timing assertion.
